subject: 'cannot coerce class "labelled" into a data.frame' Error

messages.author: ad98d4ae9f9335d5
messages.subject: 'cannot coerce class "labelled" into a data.frame' Error
parts:
Hi,

I'm a novice re both R and ggplot2, so apologies if this is a naive
question.

I'm playing with qplot & ggplot, using toy data. I am hitting one
particular error, particularly with data imported from SPSS.

Here's a few lines from the kind of data set that causes me the
problem:

gender dosage perf
1 male zero 10
2 male zero 10
3 male zero 8
...

where gender and dosage are factors.

Then I try this to get something like a simple interaction plot:

> p <- ggplot(data=testdataset)
> p + stat_summary(fun=mean, mapping=aes(x=dosage, y=perf, colour=gender, group=gender), geom="line")

which gives me this error:

Error in as.data.frame.default(x[[i]], optional = TRUE) :
cannot coerce class "labelled" into a data.frame

One odd thing is that in an earlier R session exactly the same
commands did produce a plot without error, on exactly the same data
set (though I didn't keep my R history, so perhaps there's a subtle
difference I'm missing).

Any idea what I might be doing wrong?

Cheers,

CB.

messages.subject: Re: 'cannot coerce class "labelled" into a data.frame' Error
parts:
Hi Hadley,

OK, thanks. It's not now a practical problem for me as I've found I
can work around it using a different method of going from spss to R,
using csv as the interchange format rather than por. I am puzzled
though, hence I'll continue to investigate.

The reproducible bit is difficult, as the error seems intermittent,
albeit intractable during the sessions it does occur.

The dataset was created using 'testdataset = spss.get
("testdataset.sav")' from, with spss.get Hmisc.

The structure is as follows:

> class(testdataset)
[1] "data.frame"
> class(testdataset$gender)
[1] "labelled" "factor"
> class(testdataset$dosage)
[1] "labelled" "factor"
> class(testdataset$perf)
[1] "labelled"
>

I'm enough of an R newbie not to know about "labelled" as a class,
and haven't found it yet in the docs.

This morning the problem isn't occurring (ie. now the plot just
works), but from past precedent I guess it will occur again, in which
case I'll pursue it further.

Cheers,

CB.
